title: Hull City 2-0 Brighton: McBurnie's late heroics snatch dramatic victory
subtitle: Hull City put in a superb defensive performance to frustrate Brighton, but took advantage of a late red card to secure a last-gasp win.
paragraphs: Oli McBurnie secured Hull City a dramatic 2-0 win over 10-man Brighton in the Premier League with two stoppage-time goals.

The game looked to be heading for a goalless draw after Konstantinos Tzolakis frustrated Brighton's attack, but when Costinha was sent off late on, Hull took advantage, with McBurnie producing a heroic late effort to get the Tigers back to winning ways.
Brighton were on top in the early stages, and Diego Gomez ghosted in behind Hull's defence to meet Maxim De Cuyper's low cross, but Tzolakis smothered the chance from point-blank range.
Tzolakis had a busy first half, with a string of saves, including sticking out a leg to keep out Georginio Rutter's low strike.
Yasin Ayari then crashed Gomez's pullback against the crossbar, and Rutter followed in, but Hull's goalkeeper rushed out to get a strong left hand behind the rebound.
And Tzolakis was alert again just before the break, getting the slightest touch on Gomez's shot to deflect it behind, while the Paraguayan also curled an effort wide shortly after the break.
Mohamed Belloumi provided an outlet down the right and saw two counter-attacks end in chances; he sent one straight at Bart Verbruggen and dragged the other agonisingly wide.

Sorba Thomas also hit the crossbar with a floated cross from the other wing, though Regan Slater almost gifted Brighton the win with a loose backpass. He recovered to clear it off the line behind Tzolakis.

But Costinha earned himself a needless second booking in the 89th minute after dragging back Thomas, and it proved very costly for the visitors. Hull broke quickly on the counter again, with Lucas Gourna-Douath touching it into McBurnie, who guided it home through a crowd of bodies in the 92nd minute.
Brighton continued to commit bodies forward, and when Belloumi flicked it past his defender to race down the right again, he squared it into McBurnie for a simple 95th-minute tap-in.
Hull dig in deep with dogged win

Brighton are the league's highest scorers, and they had the chance to move within three points of leaders Arsenal with a win at MKM Stadium, but they were largely frustrated by Hull's admirable defensive showing.
In fact, goalkeeper Tzolakis, who made seven saves, had the most touches of any Hull player (41) while he also attempted the most passes (28).
It is only the third time the Greece international has made as many saves in a league game in which he has kept a clean sheet during his career, but the first time with Hull.

The Tigers have made their home a difficult place to come since their promotion, remaining unbeaten at MKM Stadium this term (W2 D4); it is their longest unbeaten start at home in a league campaign since 2015-16 (first eight).

Brighton had largely dominated, accruing 2.24 expected goals (xG), with 1.75 of that coming before the break. They had 15 shots in total to Hull's 11, but the hosts always looked like they could provide a sting.

It is the first time since 2009 Hull have won a game via a 90th-minute goal, while it is the first time they have scored two such goals in a single Premier League game. Brighton had never conceded twice in the 90th minute before either.
And it was all down to McBurnie, who netted his first brace in the competition on his 107th appearance.
